intro.title: useCallback for Stable References
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that demonstrates how to use the `useCallback` hook to create stable function references. You will learn how `useCallback` helps prevent unnecessary re-renders by memoizing functions, ensuring they remain the same across renders unless their dependencies change. The core concepts covered include function memoization, dependency arrays, and optimizing performance in reactive components. You'll work with Vue's Composition API, specifically the `useCallback` hook, within a Vue single-file component using JavaScript.
intro.usecase: In real Vue applications, stable callback references are essential for performance optimization in interactive components like data dashboards with dynamic filters. When users adjust date ranges, category selectors, or search inputs, these callbacks are passed to child components that should only re-render when their actual props change. Without useCallback, every parent re-render would create new function references, causing unnecessary child re-renders in components like sortable tables, chart controls, or complex form validators. This pattern is particularly valuable in admin panels where multiple filtering components need to maintain stable identities for Vue's reactivity system to work efficiently.
